value.text: Orion must raise an operator escalation when three dead-letter events occur for the same tenant within one hour, measured from the first of the three events.
A worker may renew its lease every thirty seconds while work is progressing, and a renewal extends the lease by the full lease duration from the moment of renewal.

While a job is active, a further delivery is ignored only when it has both the same job id and the same idempotency key; the same job id with a different key is rejected as conflicting input and must not change the active job's state.
A job must be executed at most three times in total, including the first execution; after the third execution ends without success, no further execution may be started.
One original execution may be followed by at most three retry executions; once three retries have ended without success, the job must not be executed again.
The first retry waits two seconds from the failed execution; each later retry waits twice the previous wait, never exceeding thirty seconds.
After cancellation, no future execution attempt may be started; a running attempt is not interrupted; a repeated cancellation of an already-cancelled job leaves it cancelled and otherwise unchanged.
Before every retry the worker must wait exactly five seconds from the end of the failed attempt, and the wait must not vary with attempt number.
When the per-execution time limit is reached, the execution must be stopped and recorded as a failed attempt.
FIFO execution order is guaranteed only among jobs in the same queue partition; no ordering guarantee is made between jobs in different partitions.

A worker must renew when twenty seconds of lease life remain if work is progressing, must not renew the same lease more often than once every fifteen seconds, and a renewal extends the lease by the full lease duration from the moment of renewal.
While a job id is active, any further delivery with the same job id must be ignored and must not change the active job's state.
After the final unsuccessful execution attempt, Orion must automatically move the job to the dead-letter queue, and a dead-lettered job must not be executed again unless explicitly resubmitted.

EV-O-A01.content:
## 1. Execution attempts

Every job admitted to Orion is executed by a worker. An execution attempt is one delivery of the job to a worker that either succeeds, fails, or times out. Orion bounds the number of attempts so that a job that cannot succeed does not consume worker capacity forever.

Normative rule
1. A job must be executed at most three times in total.
2. The first execution counts as one of the three.
3. When the third execution has ended without success, no further execution of that job may be started.

Example
A job whose first two executions fail is executed a third time. If that execution also fails, the job has exhausted its attempts.

EV-O-B01.content:
## 2. Retry delay

After an execution attempt fails, Orion waits before delivering the job again. The wait gives transient downstream faults time to clear without hammering the dependency that just failed.

Normative rule
1. Before every retry attempt the worker must wait exactly five seconds, measured from the end of the failed attempt.
2. The wait must not be shortened or lengthened based on the attempt number.

Example
An attempt fails at 10:00:00. The next attempt may start no earlier than 10:00:05. If that attempt also fails at 10:00:20, the following attempt may start no earlier than 10:00:25.

## Execution — delay before a retry

Normative rule
1. Before every retry attempt the worker must wait exactly five seconds, measured from the end of the failed attempt.
2. The wait must not be shortened or lengthened based on the attempt number.

Example
Q-31's initial execution fails at 08:14:10; the first retry starts no earlier than 08:14:15. Each later retry likewise starts no earlier than five seconds after the preceding failure.

EV-O-B05.content:
## Execution — delay before a retry

Once an execution has failed, Orion pauses before delivering the job again so that a transient fault downstream has a chance to clear. The pause grows with each failure so that a dependency under sustained pressure is not retried at a fixed cadence.

Normative rule
1. Before the first retry of a job the worker must wait two seconds, measured from the end of the failed execution.
2. Before each later retry the worker must wait twice as long as it waited before the previous retry.
3. The wait before any retry must never exceed thirty seconds.

Example
Q-31 fails at 08:14:10. Its first retry starts no earlier than 08:14:12; if that fails at 08:14:20 the second retry starts no earlier than 08:14:24; a subsequent wait would be eight seconds, then sixteen, then thirty (the cap).

EV-O-C01.content:
## 3. Attempt timeout

A worker that hangs must not hold a job indefinitely. Each attempt is bounded by a timeout after which the attempt is treated as failed and the retry policy applies.

Normative rule
1. Each execution attempt must time out after thirty seconds of execution.
2. An attempt that reaches the timeout must be recorded as a failed attempt.

Example
An attempt starts at 12:00:00 and has not completed by 12:00:30. Orion records the attempt as failed at 12:00:30.

EV-O-C02.content:
## 3. Attempt timeout

A worker that hangs must not hold a job indefinitely. Each attempt is bounded by a timeout after which the attempt is treated as failed and the retry policy applies.

Normative rule
1. An individual execution may run for no longer than half a minute; when that limit is reached the execution must be stopped.
2. An execution stopped at the limit must be recorded as a failed attempt.

Example
An execution starts at 12:00:00 and is still running at 12:00:30. Orion stops it and records a failed attempt at 12:00:30.

EV-O-D01.content:
## 4. Duplicate delivery

Producers may deliver the same job more than once, for example after a network timeout on the producer side. Orion must not execute a job twice because of such redelivery.

Normative rule
1. While a job with a given job id is active, any further delivery carrying the same job id must be ignored.
2. Ignoring a duplicate delivery must not change the state of the active job.

Example
Job J-17 is delivered at 09:00 and is executing. A second delivery of J-17 arrives at 09:01 and is ignored; J-17 continues unaffected.

EV-O-D10.content:
## Input handling — repeated deliveries

A producer that times out may send the same job again, but two deliveries that share a job id are not necessarily the same request: a producer may reuse a job id for different payloads. Orion therefore uses the idempotency key to decide whether a repeat is genuinely the same request.

Normative rule
1. While a job with a given job id is active, a further delivery must be ignored only when it carries both the same job id and the same idempotency key as the active job.
2. A further delivery that carries the same job id but a different idempotency key must be rejected as conflicting input and must not change the state of the active job.

Example
Q-52 (key IK-1) is delivered at 11:00 and is active. A delivery of Q-52 with key IK-1 at 11:02 is ignored. A delivery of Q-52 with key IK-2 at 11:03 is rejected as conflicting.

## Input handling — repeated deliveries

A producer that times out may send the same job again, but two deliveries that share a job id are not necessarily the same request: a producer may reuse a job id for different payloads. Orion therefore uses the idempotency key to decide whether a repeat is genuinely the same request.

Normative rule
1. While a job with a given job id is active, a further delivery must be ignored only when it carries both the same job id and the same idempotency key as the active job.
2. A further delivery that carries the same job id but a different idempotency key must be rejected as conflicting input and must not change the state of the active job.

Example
Q-52 (key IK-1) is delivered at 11:00 and is active. A delivery of Q-52 with key IK-1 at 11:02 is ignored. A delivery of Q-52 with key IK-2 at 11:03 is rejected as conflicting.

## 5. Idempotency keys

Each delivery may carry an idempotency key chosen by the producer. Orion remembers keys for a bounded period so that repeated deliveries with the same key can be recognised.

Normative rule
1. Orion must retain each idempotency key for twenty-four hours after it is first seen.
2. After the retention period the key may be forgotten and a later delivery with the same key is treated as new.

Example
Key K-9 is first seen on Monday at 08:00. A delivery with K-9 on Monday at 20:00 is recognised as a repeat. A delivery with K-9 on Tuesday at 09:00 is treated as new.

## 6. Worker lease

A worker that receives a job holds a lease on it. The lease is how Orion knows that the job is being worked on and prevents a second worker from taking it.

Normative rule
1. A worker lease must last sixty seconds from the moment the job is delivered to the worker.
2. When the lease expires without renewal or release, the job must become available to other workers.

Example
A worker receives job J-4 at 14:00:00 and neither renews nor releases it. At 14:01:00 the lease expires and J-4 may be delivered to another worker.

## 8. Cancellation

A producer or operator may cancel a job. Cancellation stops Orion from investing further effort in the job, but Orion does not forcibly abort work that a worker is already performing.

Normative rule
1. After a job is cancelled, no future execution attempt of that job may be started.
2. Cancellation must not interrupt an execution attempt that is already running; that attempt runs to its own completion, failure or timeout.

Example
Job J-8 is cancelled while its second attempt is running. The second attempt continues; when it ends, no third attempt is started.

Example

JDG-222b99f8-0111-4095-b0f0-fa6608906b55.rationale: EV-O-E13 requires each idempotency key to be retained for twenty-four hours after first seen, after which a later delivery with that key is treated as new.

value.text: A worker must renew when twenty seconds of lease life remain if work is progressing, must not renew the same lease more often than once every fifteen seconds, and a renewal extends the lease by the full lease duration from the moment of renewal.

JDG-2cabf51b-9bef-4ab7-8c34-28f7ee87317e.rationale: EV-O-G13 requires renewal at twenty seconds remaining, rate-limits renewal to once per fifteen seconds, and extends by the full lease duration.

JDG-2d6e8972-1af8-4ed9-9f3f-1f08fb7d7e4a.rationale: EV-O-A13 caps how many times a job may run: one original execution plus at most three retries, after which the job must not be executed again.

value.text: The first retry waits two seconds from the failed execution; each later retry waits twice the previous wait, never exceeding thirty seconds.

JDG-31219b4c-a10a-476f-b5f3-871197d37467.rationale: EV-O-B05 and EV-O-B07 specify exponential backoff from two seconds, doubling each retry and capped at thirty seconds.

value.text: FIFO execution order is guaranteed only among jobs in the same queue partition; no ordering guarantee is made between jobs in different partitions.

JDG-3b9aa0f9-8032-40c0-8a88-bf981e749c03.rationale: EV-O-K13 limits the FIFO guarantee to jobs in the same partition and makes no ordering promise across partitions.

JDG-400e129e-5e64-433f-af36-b96f7cba2409.rationale: EV-O-F13 requires a worker lease to last ninety seconds from delivery and the job to become available to other workers if the lease expires without renewal or release.

JDG-4088a634-5637-432c-bb7c-fbfc2631a58a.rationale: EV-O-G13 specifies when a progressing worker must renew, a fifteen-second minimum between renewals, and that a renewal extends the lease by the full duration.

JDG-524ee01a-2b97-4375-ba0b-1511ab513f10.rationale: EV-O-F13 requires a worker lease to last ninety seconds from the moment the job is delivered to the worker.

value.text: After the final unsuccessful execution attempt, Orion must automatically move the job to the dead-letter queue, and a dead-lettered job must not be executed again unless explicitly resubmitted.

JDG-561f5335-1b5a-43c3-a4f9-800482778bc5.rationale: EV-O-I13 requires automatic dead-lettering after the last failed attempt and forbids further execution unless the job is explicitly resubmitted.

JDG-59c10453-9f19-49af-89f1-8e2cc8ff2b0b.rationale: EV-O-H13 states that cancellation blocks future attempts without aborting a running attempt, and that a repeated cancellation leaves the job cancelled without other state change.

value.text: Orion must raise an operator escalation when three dead-letter events occur for the same tenant within one hour, measured from the first of the three events.

JDG-63567828-4a4c-4c29-8838-d9b8b3c793a7.rationale: EV-O-J13 escalates at three dead-letter events for one tenant within a one-hour window starting at the first event.

value.text: While a job is active, a further delivery is ignored only when it has both the same job id and the same idempotency key; the same job id with a different key is rejected as conflicting input and must not change the active job's state.

JDG-72322170-97c7-45d5-8a0a-8a906460f253.rationale: EV-O-D13 ignores a repeat only when job id and idempotency key both match, and rejects a same-id different-key delivery as conflicting without changing state.

JDG-841aca0a-fd00-411f-bbad-6116fb588966.rationale: EV-O-C13 bounds each execution to half a minute and requires a stop at that limit to be recorded as a failed attempt.

value.text: Before every retry the worker must wait exactly five seconds from the end of the failed attempt, and the wait must not vary with attempt number.

JDG-9831079f-9ff3-49e7-b6e5-59e267aa9d65.rationale: EV-O-B13 requires a fixed five-second wait before every retry, independent of attempt number.

JDG-a640aa48-dc15-4924-865c-2616d0111109.rationale: EV-O-B13 requires a fixed five-second wait before every retry, measured from the end of the failed attempt and independent of attempt number.

JDG-ade299b1-198b-429f-a4c4-e8ee6a3a52b8.rationale: EV-O-J13 requires an operator escalation when three dead-letter events occur for the same tenant within one hour measured from the first of those events.

value.text: After cancellation, no future execution attempt may be started; a running attempt is not interrupted; a repeated cancellation of an already-cancelled job leaves it cancelled and otherwise unchanged.

JDG-b3ce22fa-3275-4af0-832e-df03e52bedeb.rationale: EV-O-H13 forbids later attempts after cancel, leaves a running attempt to finish on its own, and treats a repeated cancellation as a no-op on job state.

JDG-b5d76e95-6796-4837-a800-e587e4338532.rationale: EV-O-C13 limits an individual execution to half a minute and the example treats 12:00:00 to 12:00:30 as that limit.

value.text: One original execution may be followed by at most three retry executions; once three retries have ended without success, the job must not be executed again.

JDG-bdafd117-729f-488d-b892-967982f9a9f5.rationale: EV-O-A13 allows one original execution plus no more than three retries, and forbids further execution after the third retry fails.

JDG-c00d6c4e-4953-48b7-a5ee-a353a7d1137d.rationale: EV-O-L13 requires audit history to remain queryable for thirty calendar days from recording, after which an event may be deleted.

value.text: A job must be executed at most three times in total, including the first execution; after the third execution ends without success, no further execution may be started.

JDG-ce30a880-fc5a-4475-acb1-51236143e623.rationale: EV-O-A01 and EV-O-A02 require at most three executions in total, with the first counting as one of the three.

JDG-de22cfc3-96b3-41f9-826e-804ce85fcedc.rationale: EV-O-K13 guarantees first-in-first-out execution only among jobs in the same queue partition and makes no ordering promise across partitions.

JDG-eb0817d8-4e14-4f99-b430-dd9d658c65ec.rationale: EV-O-E13 requires each idempotency key to be retained for twenty-four hours after it is first seen.

value.text: When the per-execution time limit is reached, the execution must be stopped and recorded as a failed attempt.

JDG-f7674ff4-2dc1-4afa-9b62-f4fc7e5c3901.rationale: EV-O-C13 requires that an execution reaching the limit is stopped and recorded as a failed attempt.

JDG-f7e64cca-0661-4275-98ac-fe1297414532.rationale: EV-O-F01 and EV-O-F06 require a worker lease to last sixty seconds from delivery to the worker.

value.text: While a job id is active, any further delivery with the same job id must be ignored and must not change the active job's state.

JDG-fa84a1bd-7131-4f68-85e3-9c2559fc3a18.rationale: EV-O-D01 and EV-O-D09 ignore any further delivery that carries the same job id while that job is active, without changing its state.
